note: Rows the main session added after the agent sweeps. From data/research/datacenter_bills.json, with duplicates of held events dropped.

people.name: Gabe Evans
people.position: Lead House sponsor of the Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340); says states should keep flexibility over rate design.
key_actions: Offered the committee substitute narrowing it to data centers

quote.text: My bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act ensures large data centers pay for the infrastructure they require while giving states the flexibility to determine what works best for their communities.

people.name: Kathy Castor
people.position: Democratic co-lead of H.R. 9340; calls it a first step that lets states set stricter guardrails.

quote.text: The bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act is an important first step that can help lower costs for our neighbors back home and empower states to set additional, strict guardrails.

people.name: Jon Husted
people.position: Senate sponsor of S. 5028 and leader of the push to pass H.R. 9340; in a competitive 2026 race against Sherrod Brown where data centers are an issue.
key_actions: Pushed leaders to hold the 2026-09-30 cloture vote

quote.text: In plain language, if you create the cost, you should pay the cost.

people.name: Brian Fitzpatrick
people.position: Cosponsor of H.R. 9340; also backs the Data Center Transparency Act (H.R. 6984) and a Data Center Bill of Rights resolution (H.Res. 1471).

quote.text: The Ratepayer Protection Act addresses who pays

people.name: Josh Hawley
people.position: Lead sponsor of the GRID Act; wants data centers on their own power and public reporting of their electricity use.

quote.text: American families should not have to shoulder the burden of the rising electricity costs produced by data centers in Missouri and across the country.

people.name: Chris Van Hollen
people.position: Lead sponsor of the Power for the People Act; wants FERC-run data center load queues and data center rate classes.

quote.text: the huge corporations building and running data centers should cover the costs of the energy they need – not push those costs onto the backs of consumers

people.name: Paul Tonko
people.position: House lead of the Power for the People Act (H.R. 8241); told the Energy and Commerce markup the committee bills did not go far enough.

quote.text: We are not doing what this moment demands of us,

people.name: Byron Donalds
people.role: U.S. Representative (R-FL); candidate for Florida governor
people.position: Sponsor of H.R. 9777, which would require data centers to run off the grid and off public water.

quote.text: It’s in their interest to make sure that we can construct these centers, and I think the number one way you address and mitigate the concerns that people are having is to just ensure their utility bills aren’t going up in the process.

people.name: Lisa Blunt Rochester
people.position: Lead Democratic sponsor of the Senate Data Center Transparency Act of 2026.
key_actions: 2026-10-01: Introduced the Data Center Transparency Act of 2026 with Sen. Curtis

quote.text: there is legitimate concern about how these projects could raise utility bills, harm our environment, or impact public health

people.name: John Curtis
people.position: Republican co-lead of the Senate Data Center Transparency Act of 2026.
key_actions: 2026-10-01: Introduced the Data Center Transparency Act of 2026 with Sen. Blunt Rochester

quote.text: Americans are rightly skeptical when a large company tells them not to worry about the impacts of a new data center in their community,
